subject: Nanotechnology
title: Labeling Nano Products
description: Learn Labeling Nano Products in one minute.

hook.text: Does your sunscreen contain nano? In Europe, the label must say so. In the US, it does not have to.

buildup.text: EU cosmetics regulation requires [nano] after any nano-ingredient on the label — transparency by law.

discovery.text: Labeling empowers consumers to choose — and drives manufacturers to justify or replace nano ingredients.

twist.text: The label does not explain risk — consumers may fear [nano] without understanding that most nano cosmetics are safe.

climax.text: Smart labels with QR codes linking to safety data could bridge the gap between transparency and understanding.

punchline.text: A label saying [nano] informs — but education must follow for it to help.

quiz.question: Why can mandatory nano labeling sometimes backfire?
options: Consumers may fear the [nano] label without understanding that most nano cosmetics are safe
Labels are too small to read on cosmetic packaging
